title: Guess two thirds of the average
hook: Guess two thirds of everyone's average. If everyone reasons perfectly, what wins?

knows: a dominated choice is never best
doesNotKnow: that if everyone is rational and knows it, deleting dominated choices round after round leaves only 0

misconception: The rational guess is about 33 (two thirds of an average of 50).
objective: The learner can explain that guesses above 66.7 always do worse than 66.7, that each round of 'everyone knows that' cuts the ceiling by a third (44.4, 29.6, ...), and that with any real number allowed only 0 survives every round.

claims.text: Because the average is at most 100, the target is at most 66.7, so any guess above 66.7 always does worse than guessing 66.7.
claims.source: Target t = (2/3) x average <= 200/3 = 66.67. For x > 66.67 >= t, |66.67 - t| < |x - t|. Same step at each round with the previous ceiling.

claims.text: After k rounds of deleting such guesses the ceiling is 100 × (2/3)^k: 66.7, 44.4, 29.6, ...; it falls below 33 at round 3 and under 1 at round 12.
claims.source: Builder's node script (scratchpad ncm-e01-checks/check.mjs): [100, 66.667, 44.444, 29.63, 19.753, 13.169, 8.779, 5.853, 3.902, 2.601, 1.734, 1.156, 0.771]; first value < 1 at k = 12. Demo.tsx ceiling, PAST_33, UNDER_1. The lesson does not say the bound reaches 0 after any finite number of rounds.

claims.text: With any real number from 0 to 100 allowed, the only guess that survives every round is 0.
claims.source: Every x > 0 exceeds 100 x (2/3)^k for large enough k, so it is deleted; 0 is never above a positive ceiling. Requires real-valued guesses: with whole numbers only, 1 survives (at all-1s the target is 0.67, nearer to 1 than to 0), as the brief's edit notes. The stage says 'decimals allowed'.

claims.text: The 0 answer needs everyone to be rational and to know that everyone else is, round after round; without that, the best guess changes.
claims.source: Each deletion round uses one more level of 'everyone knows everyone is rational'. If others' guesses average m > 0, the best reply is (2/3)m (for a negligible own effect), which is not 0. No empirical claim about how real people guess is made (Nagel 1995 is flagged for a human source check and kept out of learner text).

recall.question: Everyone picks any number from 0 to 100 and the closest to 2/3 of the average wins. If all are rational and know everyone is, what is picked?
recall.why: Above 66.7 can never be best; once everyone knows that, above 44.4 can't either, and so on. Each round cuts a third, and only 0 survives them all.
